elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI specifying the Termination Date." There are no Order Forms in this hosting agreement, so an Order-Form limb is unnecessary.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Company right runs on "ninety (90) days written notice," which exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling. To reach preferred the drafter would have to state 30 days or fewer.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language appears anywhere in the rendered text; Section 3.1 is a monthly Net Sales revenue share paid in arrears, but no operative pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts was added, so the element is unaddressed as drafted.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as amended: "provided that a Termination Date specified by HDI shall be the end of the then-current term." The effective date of any HDI termination is expressly tied to term end, so HDI's exit is natural-term non-renewal rather than a mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI specifying the Termination Date" — an express, unconditional Customer election at 90 days, inside the 60–90 day band.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) as amended: "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the amounts payable by the Company under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." The Termination Payment is the only early-exit charge, the cap basis is the Company's Section 3.1 compensation (a defined amount), and the measurement window is three months.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The Section 4.1 proviso fixes any HDI-specified Termination Date at "the end of the then-current term," expressly tying the effective date to term end rather than leaving HDI free to self-date a mid-term exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 4.1 language: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — HDI's notice obligation is 90 days and is unchanged by the edits.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (express 90-day Company convenience right; HDI Termination Date fixed at term end; Termination Payment capped at three months of Section 3.1 amounts; HDI's retained 90-day notice).

Preferred level fails on two elements — the Company notice period is 90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees was added — but that is immaterial because the fallback checklist is fully satisfied.

Minimality holds: exactly three surgical edits, each traceable to a distinct unmet fallback element (Vendor term-end proviso, new Customer convenience sentence, cap proviso). No deletions, no survival tails, no added procedures, no 'in whole or in part' surplus (there are no Order Forms), and the favourable retained mechanics in 4.2(b)–(c) are untouched.

Intent preserved: the Termination Payment formula, the $800,000 deduction, the zero floor and quarterly instalments all continue to operate beneath the new ceiling; the cap basis references an existing defined section (3.1) so no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and the 'Termination Date' definition still functions for both parties.

Claimed finding status of 'deviation' is correct on the original text: the pre-edit clause let HDI self-date a mid-term walk-away and exposed the Company to an uncapped Net Sales-based Termination Payment, both material fallback failures.
